newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to sell Fesilven in second quarter 1997.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to sell Fesilven in second quarter 1997.

text.p: The Venezuelan Investment Fund (FIV) expects to sell ferro-silica producer Fesilven in the second quarter of 1997, a FIV official told Reuters Monday.
"We hope that Fesilven's privatization will be carried out more or less in April or May next year," said the official, who asked not to be named.

The FIV announced Monday that it was extending the date for registering interest in Fesilven from November 27 to December 11 at the request of potential bidders. Qualified bidders will be announced on December 13, the official said.
Those interested in bidding must be able to meet requirements including a minimum net worth of $25 million and a ferro-silica production capacity of more than 30,000 metric tonnes per year.
U.S. investment bank Salomon Brothers is coordinating the sale, which will set aside between 10 and 20 percent of the company's stock for workers.
Founded in 1973, Fesilven has three ovens that produce 80,000 metric tonnes of ferro-silica per year. In 1995, it produced about three percent of the world's ferro-silica.
